items.prompt: Why is the exercise's sqrt(252) scaling not a universal theorem for arbitrary serially dependent returns?

options.text: The number 252 can never be used in a financial model.
options.why: It is a valid stated exercise convention; the issue is unsupported generalization.

options.text: Basis points and percentages cannot be converted.
options.why: They are convertible units; dependence affects time aggregation.

options.text: Every return series has independent days by definition.
options.why: Independence is a model assumption, not a consequence of calling observations daily.

options.text: Cross-day covariance can change the variance of aggregated returns.
options.why: A simple square-root rule needs assumptions beyond this sample-statistic computation.

items.explanation: A simple square-root rule needs assumptions beyond this sample-statistic computation.
